title: Canada - Best Sim?
body:
O.P.
Hi All,
We are off to Canada later in the year for 5 weeks. I'm keen to find out best Sim options, both Physical and ESim.
We will also be in Japan for 5 days on the way back so if a sim option can be used in both countries that is great but happy to get a different Sim for our stint in Japan.
Cheers, Pok

---- replies ----
[User #6732931441 postsWindy HillWhirlpool Enthusiast] Rogers best coverage. You will find all sims over there expensive, with very low data allowances.
[User #535192244 poststhebookfreak58Whirlpool Forums Addict] I used airalo e-sim. Might not be the cheapest but worked fine. Uses Canada Mobile network. Rogers seemed to have better coverage but not by a huge amount.
[User #360621420 postswatcher-0000Forum Regular] Windy Hill writes...
You will find all sims over there expensive, with very low data allowances.
Pricing is much better than it used to be. I've been coming to Canada regularly for 35 years.
One option is PhoneBox – they resell Rogers/Telus – you can buy an esim online. My daughter has just used PhoneBox with 75GB for $41CAD for 30 days (I think it connected via Telus).
As stated Rogers is expensive – their sub-brand, FIDO, is cheaper but uses the Rogers network.

Hey all,
Any other recommendations?
We will be in Canada for 35/36 days ... and then Japan for 6/7 days if that makes a difference.
Phonebox ( welcome.phoneboxmobile.ca ) for Canada at $35CAD for 30 days 75gb, unlimited Canada calling, ulimited international sms and 1000 mins international mins calling seems pretty good .... open to other suggestions though
Cheers, Pok
[User #1763818231 postsTicTacToetrained chickenWhirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
pokolbinguy writes...
Any other recommendations?
It’s highly unlikely the best value will be one coverall SIM for Canada and Japan – just get one for each. I’m on Airolo for both (I’m also stopping in Japan on the way home). As someone said – Airolo uses Canada Mobile . Apparently this is a Airolo quirk with the network name showing generically – there is no “Canada Mobile”. They use Bell. My Optus SIM is on with data roaming off for SMS receiving, and it’s on Rogers so I can see them side by side – although the internet says Rogers is the best in western Canada, I haven’t seen any material difference. They both lose coverage in roughly the same places, where there’s no mobile service at all.
Neither country is that great with physical SIMs for tourists – both countries have a legacy of poorly serving this market, but eSIMs for both are easy and simple. It’s not like other regions with deep histories of serving the tourist market with dedicated SIMs.
You’ll have to compare pricing with your own parameters – I don’t need voice calling or local numbers, my length of stay is different and I used a coupon code that’s no longer current and I did my purchasing a month or too back.
[User #6759712844 postsdarktranqPuck MadWhirlpool Forums Addict] pokolbinguy writes...
$35CAD for 30 days 75gb, unlimited Canada calling, ulimited international sms and 1000 mins international mins calling seems pretty good
Because that's exceptional to be honest. It used to be a LOT more expensive.
[User #2599603453 postsTommiMWhirlpool Forums Addict] We went with TravelKon as I need a physical SIM. I think it was $40 for 10GB over 30 days.
It worked well in the cities, but then I had to switch to roaming (which was limited) in Newfoundland, I think most of us didn't get much coverage up there anyway.
That Phonebox deal looks great, just need to make sure you do it early enough for the SIM to arrive in Australia (if you need a physical SIM). The one place you are going to want coverage is at the airport when you arrive, don't forget to take one of those opening pins with you. (also, it looks like you might need to remember to cancel it when you leave?)

Any one else with any insights on other deals?
In regards to this deal that I found;
welcome.phoneboxmobile.ca
I had a look at the buying / setup process and seems they have a set "billing cycle" (e.g start to end of month) BUT when you put in your activation dates it pro-rata's the charge for the balance of the current month PLUS the following month, which for me works very well as we land late in the initial month and depart right at the end.
We land in Vancouver on 26/7 and depart 30/8.
The "set billing period" shown is 2/8 – 1/9 for the $35/month plus the initial pro-rata of 26/7 – 1/8 of $7.90 = $42.90 ... plus 12% taxes so $48.04 for our 36 days and 92gb to use in that period.
Works out to equivilent to $38 / month for 75gb which is the same as a local Aussie Aldi plan for the same inclusions.
